title: The Holy Trinity
summary: One God in three Persons: what the Bible teaches, how the church confessed it, and why it matters.
description: The doctrine of the Trinity is at the heart of the Christian faith. This course shows from Scripture that there is one God, that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are each fully God, and that they are distinct Persons. It explains how the early church guarded this truth against error, and how the Trinity shapes salvation, prayer, worship and Christian life.
objectives: Show from Scripture that there is only one God
Show the full deity and distinct personhood of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Explain the historic creeds and the errors they rejected
Apply the doctrine of the Trinity to salvation and daily life
outcomes: State the doctrine of the Trinity in one clear sentence
Give Bible evidence for the deity of the Son and of the Spirit
Explain the role of the Council of Nicaea
Describe how each Person of the Trinity works in salvation

modules.title: There Is One God
modules.intro: The Bible's first great confession is that God is one. The Trinity never means three gods.

lessons.title: Hear, O Israel
lessons.body:
Israel lived among nations with many gods. God revealed that He alone is God: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD" (Deuteronomy 6:4). "I am the LORD, and there is none else, there is no God beside me" (Isaiah 45:5).

The New Testament repeats this truth. Jesus quoted the Shema as the first commandment (Mark 12:29). Paul says, "there is none other God but one" (1 Corinthians 8:4), and James, "Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well" (James 2:19).

Christians are monotheists: we worship one God only.

lessons.title: Hints in the Old Testament
lessons.body:
Though the Old Testament stresses God's oneness, it also hints at plurality within the one God.

God says, "Let us make man in our image" (Genesis 1:26). The "angel of the LORD" speaks as God and is called God (Genesis 16:10-13; Exodus 3:2-6). The Spirit of God moves on the waters (Genesis 1:2). In Isaiah 48:16 the speaker says, "the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me."

These hints become clear only in the light of the New Testament, when the Son is made flesh and the Spirit is poured out.

lessons.title: What the Trinity is and is not
lessons.body:
The doctrine of the Trinity can be summed up in three statements:

1. There is one God.
2. The Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God.
3. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are distinct Persons.

The Trinity does **not** mean three gods (tritheism), or one Person wearing three masks (modalism). God is one in **essence** (being) and three in **Persons**.

The word "Trinity" is not in the Bible, but the truth it names is. Jesus commands baptism "in the name" (singular) "of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 28:19).

An Old Testament figure who speaks as God and is often seen as a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son.

modules.title: The Father, the Son and the Spirit
modules.intro: This week we see that each Person is fully God, and that each is distinct from the others.

lessons.title: The Father is God; the Son is God
lessons.body:
No one disputes that the Father is God (John 6:27; Ephesians 4:6).

The New Testament clearly calls the Son God. "The Word was God" (John 1:1). Thomas worshipped Him: "My Lord and my God" (John 20:28). Paul calls Him "God blessed for ever" (Romans 9:5), and Hebrews says the Father addresses the Son: "Thy throne, O God, is for ever" (Hebrews 1:8).

Jesus does what only God does: forgives sins (Mark 2:5-7), receives worship (Matthew 14:33), creates and upholds all things (Colossians 1:16-17), and claims the divine name "I am" (John 8:58).

lessons.title: The Holy Spirit is God
lessons.body:
The Holy Spirit is not a force but a Person, and He is God.

Peter told Ananias he had lied "to the Holy Ghost", and then, "thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God" (Acts 5:3-4). The Spirit has divine qualities: He is eternal (Hebrews 9:14), everywhere present (Psalm 139:7), and knows the deep things of God (1 Corinthians 2:10-11).

He acts as a Person: He teaches (John 14:26), speaks (Acts 13:2), can be grieved (Ephesians 4:30) and intercedes (Romans 8:26).

lessons.title: Three distinct Persons
lessons.body:
The Persons are distinct, not the same Person in different roles.

At Jesus' baptism, the Son is in the water, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father speaks from heaven (Matthew 3:16-17). Jesus prays to the Father (John 17:1), and says the Father will send "another Comforter" (John 14:16). The Father loves the Son (John 3:35).

They relate to one another in eternal love and fellowship. The Son is eternally begotten of the Father (John 1:18), and the Spirit proceeds from the Father and is sent by the Son (John 15:26).

summary: The Father is God, the Son is God, the Holy Spirit is God.

modules.title: Guarding the Truth
modules.intro: The early church faced teachings that denied the Trinity. This week we learn the errors and the creeds that answered them.

lessons.title: Three errors
lessons.body:
- **Modalism** (Sabellianism) says God is one Person who appears in three modes: sometimes as Father, sometimes as Son, sometimes as Spirit. It cannot explain Jesus praying to the Father or the baptism scene. Some modern "Jesus only" or Oneness groups hold a form of this view.
- **Arianism** says the Son is the first and highest creature, not eternal God: "there was a time when he was not." Jehovah's Witnesses teach something similar today.
- **Tritheism** says there are three separate gods.

Each error tries to make God simpler than He has revealed Himself to be.

lessons.title: Nicaea and Constantinople
lessons.body:
In AD 325 the Council of Nicaea met to answer Arius. Led by men such as Athanasius of Alexandria, the church confessed that the Son is "of one substance" (Greek *homoousios*) with the Father, "begotten, not made".

In AD 381 the Council of Constantinople expanded the creed to confess the Holy Spirit as "the Lord, the giver of life", worshipped and glorified together with the Father and the Son.

The Nicene Creed is still confessed by Christians worldwide. Athanasius, an African, stood firm when many opposed him, earning the saying "Athanasius against the world".

lessons.title: Why it matters
lessons.body:
Is the Trinity just a puzzle for scholars? No. If Jesus is not God, He could not reveal God perfectly or bear the infinite weight of our sin. If the Spirit is not God, He could not make us new or dwell in us as God's temple (1 Corinthians 6:19).

Only a triune God can be love from all eternity, before creation, because love needs someone to love: the Father has always loved the Son in the Spirit (John 17:24).

Guarding this truth guards the gospel. Every Bible-believing church, Baptist and Pentecostal alike, confesses it.

The error that there are three separate gods.

The Trinity guards the gospel and shows God as eternal love.

modules.title: The Trinity in Salvation and Life
modules.intro: The triune God saves us and draws us into His fellowship. This week we see the Trinity at work and in worship.

lessons.title: The Father plans, the Son accomplishes, the Spirit applies
lessons.body:
All three Persons work together in salvation, each in a particular way.

- The **Father** chose and sent: "God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son" (John 3:16; Ephesians 1:3-6).
- The **Son** came and redeemed us by His blood (Ephesians 1:7).
- The **Spirit** applies salvation: He regenerates, seals and indwells believers (Ephesians 1:13-14; Titus 3:5).

Peter describes believers as "elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ" (1 Peter 1:2).

lessons.title: Praying to the triune God
lessons.body:
Christian prayer is Trinitarian. We pray **to** the Father, **through** the Son, **in** the Spirit: "For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father" (Ephesians 2:18).

Jesus taught us to pray "Our Father" (Matthew 6:9), and to ask in His name (John 16:23). The Spirit helps our weakness and intercedes for us (Romans 8:26).

It is right also to worship the Son and the Spirit, for each is God. Stephen prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" (Acts 7:59).

lessons.title: Unity and love in the church
lessons.body:
Jesus prayed for His people "that they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee" (John 17:21). The unity of the Father, Son and Spirit is the pattern for the church: real unity with real difference.

Paul ties church unity to the Trinity: "one Spirit... one Lord... One God and Father of all" (Ephesians 4:4-6). Different gifts come from the same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God (1 Corinthians 12:4-6).

The church reflects the triune God when it is united in truth, humble in service and rich in love.

short.q: State the doctrine of the Trinity in your own words.
short.model: There is one God who eternally exists as three distinct Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, each fully God.

short.q: Give two Bible evidences that Jesus is God.
short.model: John 1:1 says the Word was God; Thomas called Him 'My Lord and my God'; He forgives sins, receives worship and claimed the name 'I am'.

short.q: How do we know the Holy Spirit is a Person?
short.model: He acts as a Person: He teaches, speaks, intercedes and can be grieved; He is not an impersonal force.

short.q: What is modalism, and why is it wrong?
short.model: Modalism says God is one Person appearing in three modes; it is wrong because Scripture shows the Persons as distinct, for example at Jesus' baptism and when the Son prays to the Father.

short.q: What did the Council of Nicaea confess and why?
short.model: Against Arius, Nicaea (325) confessed that the Son is of one substance with the Father, fully God, begotten not made.

short.q: Describe the work of each Person in salvation.
short.model: The Father planned and sent, the Son redeemed us by His blood, and the Spirit applies salvation by regenerating, sealing and indwelling believers.

assignments.title: Explaining the Trinity
assignments.prompt: A new believer asks, "How can Christians say there is one God, yet call Jesus God and the Spirit God?" Write a clear, simple answer with at least five Bible references, and explain why common illustrations (water, egg, one man as father, son and husband) can mislead.

assignments.title: The Trinity and my prayers
assignments.prompt: Study Ephesians 1:3-14 or Ephesians 2:18. Describe what each Person of the Trinity does for the believer, then write how this should shape your own prayer life.
